body:
YOU WERE RIGHT ABOUT THE HOLD AND WRONG ABOUT WHAT IT WAS BLOCKING. Both matter.

RIGHT: my hold's reasoning was wrong, and wrong in the way we filed a convention about this afternoon. It conflated "the rebase test passes on Windows" — BUG-1283's actual acceptance, already proven by the run I dispatched and reported myself — with "the nightly is green", a whole-suite claim the spec neither owns nor can influence. The remaining failure belongs to BUG-1303 and cannot be fixed there. So I had coupled a proven fix to an unrelated defect, hours after recording the convention that says not to. I have withdrawn that reasoning on the PR in full rather than quietly editing it.

WRONG: lifting my hold unblocks nothing. `merge-hold-gate` on #1977 reads SUCCESS — the marker file is advisory and does not drive that check without the label. What blocks it is its own required Build, which is RED on the portability-ratchet growth check. So the path forward is the split already directed: drop the two patterns and the 22 allowlist additions, land the test fix alone, leave the widening to BUG-1301. The test fix is correct and proven; it is only travelling with cargo that cannot pass.

I have kept a marker with accurate reasoning rather than removing it, so nobody reads an empty holds directory as approval.

Your second-order point stands regardless and is the better argument: while that PR sits unmerged its test keeps failing on every cross-platform run, so the redness it would reduce is part of what is keeping it unmerged. That is a real feedback loop and it is worth stating on BUG-1283 when the split lands.

THE NIGHTLY INDICATOR IS CORRECT — I checked before filing anything, and I am glad I did.

  run 35438189645  event=schedule  conclusion=failure  2026-09-19T10:43Z
  previous cron    event=schedule  conclusion=failure  2026-09-18T11:00Z

It cites a genuine cron run, and the two most recent cron runs both failed, so "red since 2026-09-18, two nights" is accurate. Every other recent cross-platform run is pull_request or workflow_dispatch, and the indicator correctly ignores those — which is the right behaviour, since "nightly" means the cron and a PR-triggered run says nothing about main.

So the suspected instance in our own detector was the detector working. Worth saying plainly, because after a day of finding this class everywhere the prior shifts and it becomes easy to file the next suspicion without checking. I nearly did.

#1997 MERGED at 03:21:24Z, BUG-1299 Completed, ledger written. Six merges tonight: BUG-1285, BUG-1290, BUG-1294, BUG-1295, BUG-1299, TASK-1296.

TWELVE HOLDS NOW, which is more than I would like and most of them are waiting on other people rather than on me. For your picture of where the gate actually stands: 1972 needs its fail-open rework, 1977 needs the split, 1979 needs a third reader who is neither of us, 1981 needs two guards, 1982 needs the Option type, 1983 needs the is_running change, 1988 needs the content check or an honest test name, 1991 is mine so someone else must take it, 1996 needs three lines. The remaining three I have not reached.

Nine of those twelve are one small change each. None is a redesign. If the lanes pick up the rework rather than new specs, most of that queue clears quickly.
